Economic offences in the country 
† *321. SHRI KAPIL SIB AL: 
SHRI RAJTV RANJAN SINGH 'LALAN1: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is fact that the number of economic offences in the country 
has increased over the years; 
(b) if not, the number of economic offences that have come to notice 
during 1998-99,1999-2000 and 2000-2001; and 
(c) the quantum of amount estimated to be involved therein alongwith the 
number of those cases where those guilty have been identified? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN): (a) No such trend is indicated by the figures. 
(b) The number of offences relating to central excise, customs duty, income-
tax (cases of concealed income of Rs. 1 crore and above) and FERA during 
1998-99,1999-2000 and 2000-2001 are 47920,49630 and 48240 respecd vely. The 
number of frauds reported by Public Sector Banks to RBI during 1998,1999 and 
2000 are 1855, 1839 and 1858 respectively. During these years, the number of 
cases of drug seizures under the NDPS Act, 1985 are 12446, 13029, and 12460 
respectively. 
(c) The amount estimated to be involved in the cases relating to central 
excise, customs duty, income tax and FERA for the years 1998-99,1999-2000 and 
2000-2001 are Rs. 3915 crore, Rs. 7879 crore and Rs. 5636 crore respectively. The 
amount involved in the cases of bank frauds during 1998, 1999 and 2000 are 
Rs. 481 crore, Rs. 537 crore and Rs. 539 crore respectively. 
The number of cases in which persons have been found guilty would not 
be known until all the appellate procedures and fora are exhausted.

Outstanding loans against businessmen/industrialists 
† *322. SHRI B ALKAVIBAIRAGI: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the number of persons, institutions, businessmen, industrialists against 
whom the amounts of loan (short term and long term) of more than Rs. one crore 
of the nationalised banks is outstanding and since when; 
(b) the amount of the interest and pena lty that have become due on the 
outstanding loan so far and what steps Government are talcing for its recovery; 
(c) whether the action to recover the outstanding amount will be taken 
against these borrowers in the same manner as is taken against common man; 
and 
(d) the details of the amount realised? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL): (a) Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reported that 
as per the available information, as on 30th September, 2000, there were 6816 
accounts in the public sector banks, with outstanding of Rs. 1 crore and above, 
which were classified as doubtful, loss and suit filed, and the total outstandings 
in these accounts was Rs. 41512.46 crores. 
(b) to (d) While the data generating system of RBI does not separately 
generate information regarding interest and penalty levied, it is included in the 
figure of total outstandings given in para (a). Government of India and Reserve 
Bank of India (RBI) have advised the banks and financial institutions to take 
several steps for recovery of bank dues such as evolving and implementation of 
recovery policy by banks, filing of suits with civil courts, filing cases with Debt 
Recovery Tribunals (DRTs), compromise settlement through Settlement Advisory 
Committees and monitoring and followup of Non- Performing Assets (NPAs) at 
various levels in the bank. RBI vide its circular dated 27th July, 2000 had framed 
non-discretionary and non-discriminatory guidelines for settlement of NPAs upto 
Rs. 5 crore and advised banks to evolve their own policy for loan outstandings of 
above.Rs. 5. crore. In various meeti ngs Government has directed the Chief 
Executives of the public sector banks to  take strictest possible action against 
wilful defaulters. Effective action by banks for rehabilitation, one-time settlement 
for filing of suits in all necessry cases by 30.9.2001 has to be ensured by the chief

Goa Airport 
*326.   SHRISANTOSHBAGRODIA: 
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the status of the plan to make the airport at Goa usable for 24 hours; 
and 
(b) by when it is going to be implemented? 
THE MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) and 
(b) Goa Airport belongs to the Ministry of Defence and is controlled by the 
Indian Navy. Airports Authority of India (AAI) only maintains a Civil Enclave at 
Goa. As Goa is an important tourist destination of the country, it was decided to 
have this airport available for civil / charter flights round the clock. A Memorandum 
of Understanding (MoU) was signed between Airports Authority of India and 
Indian Navy on 9.3.2000, to make this airport operational for 24 hours. Indian 
Navy was to procure all equipment for this purpose and AAI was to transfer Rs. 
205.72 lakhs to Indian Navy on request for this purpose. Indian Navy was also 
required to provide necessary manpower for 24 hours operation. AAI has already 
budgeted the amount. Indian Navy is obtaining necessary approvals for 110 
additional staff required for this purpose. 
Presently Goa airport operates from sunrise to sunset, except the slot from 
0830 hours to 1300 hours on Mondays to Fridays which is reserved for military 
flying. In addition, chartered tourist flights were also permitted to operate between 
0830 hours to 1300 hours on Fridays during the tourist season.

Process of tax realization 
† *327. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to introduce any scheme for improving 
the process of tax realization; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the total amount involved in tax related disputes; and 
(d) the details of the efforts made by Government for the realization of the 
disputed amount?  
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN): (a) and (b) Action to improve tax realization is 
a continuous process. Steps currently being taken include widening of tax base 
through the one by six scheme to over 4,300 towns, close monitoring of imports 
and excise checks to prevent evasion. 
(c) As on 30th June, 2001, the amount involved in central excise related 
disputes is Rs. 9287.66 crore at adjudication stage, and Rs. 8271.52 crore as 
arrears of confirmed demands. In respect of customs duty, Rs. 1937.12 crore is 
pending at adjudication stage, and Rs. 2498.57 crore is pending as arrears of 
confirmed demands. The total amount of Income Tax demands outstanding as 
on 31st March, 2001 are Rs. 59,425.17 crore. Out of this demand, the demands 
stayed/kept in abeyance, which includes demands stayed by courts/Settlement 
Commission/Income Tax Appellate Tribunal/ Income Tax authorities, is Rs. 
31,197.82 crore. 
(d) High priority is given to the work of collection/reduction of arrear 
demand and appropriate administrative, legal and other measures are taken to 
recover the same. Request is made to the concerned appellate authorities for 
early disposal of the cases. Wherever th e recovery proceedings are stayed by 
the courts, steps are initiated to get th e stays vacated. Coercive measures are 
also taken in suitable cases for speedy recovery of demand. In bigger cases, 
dossiers are maintained and the recovery position is reviewed regularly.

(i) The hydrocarbon fuels are inherently polluting and hence such fuels 
cannot be regarded as 'clean fuels' and totally non-injurious to health.

LPG and Propane can be regarded  as environmentally acceptable
